whereby the Ld. Adjudicating Officer has, inter alia, held that appellants have violated Sections 23(1), 26(1) and 26(2)
(ii) read with Section 3(1)(zf) of the FSS Act, 2006 and Regulation No. 2.2.1.3 and 2.2.2.10 of the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging & Labelling) Regulations, 2011 punishable u/s 52 of the FSS Act, 2006.

sentences.text: The allegations in brief are that on 02.11.2015, Sh. Ranjeet Singh, Food Safety Officer (FSO) had taken a sample of "Sugar Based Confectionery", an article of food for analysis from Sh. Sushil Kumar S/o Sh. Madan Lal, Food Business Operatorcum Proprietor, M/s Sharma, Confectionery, Shop No. 1, Rai Singh Market, Karari Road, Sultanpuri, Delhi110 086, where the said food article was found stored for sale for human consumption at the time of taking the sample.
The food article was available in the sealed packets having identical lable declaration upon them.
3. The sample was sent for analysis.

The Food Analyst vide his report No. FSS/992/2015 dated 07.11.2015 reported that the sample was found misbranded because there was violation of Regulation No. 2.2.1.3 and 2.2.2.10 of the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging & Labelling)
Regulations, 2011.

entities.text:
Food Safety and Standards (Packaging & Labelling)
Regulations, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Upon inquiry, it was found that the food article was supplied by appellant M/s Shellz Overseas Pvt. Ltd. and manufactured by M/s Tifosi Foods Pvt. Ltd.
4.
The report of the Food Analyst was sent to the FBO/Supplier/Manufacturer but they did not prefer any appeal against it.
5. Ld.

Adjudicating Officer after analyzing the case and hearing the parties, imposed a penalty of Rs.2,40,000/ in the ratio of 60% upon the manufacturer company, 30% upon the supplier company and 10% on FBO.
It is pertinent to mention here that the FBO did not file any appeal against it.

6. In appeal, the appellants have assailed the impugned order on the ground that the Ld.
Adjudicating Officer has passed the order in a routine manner without taking into account all the facts and circumstances of the case.
7.
Notice was issued to the respondent.

The respondent has contested the appeal and submitted that the Ld. Adjudicating Officer has passed a reasoned order after taking all the submissions of the parties and there is no illegality or impropriety therein.

8. The sample was also brought in the Court and was perused as under:
"On opening one of the brown paper/sheet, it is found containing one original sealed box of "Hugs Silky Premium Rich Cocoa Bar".

It has been observed during physical inspection of the case property being produced by the Designated Officer Sh.S.P.Singh that "Sugar Based Confectionery & Mfg.: SEP.2015" is printed at the side of the sealed box."
9.
During the course of submission, Ld. Counsel for the appellants submitted that he only wishes to challenge the order of the Ld. Adjudicating Officer to the extent of minimizing the penalty.
It has been submitted that a lenient view may be taken and the penalty amount may be reduced.
10. Per contra, Ld. Chief PP for the respondent has submitted that the Ld. Adjudicating Officer has already taken a lenient view and there is no ground for interference.

sentences.text: I have heard Sh. Sunil Kumar, Ld. Counsel for the appellants and Sh. Kundan Lal, Ld. Chief PP for the respondent and perused the record carefully.

12. Since the appellants have chosen not to challenge the order of the Ld. Adjudicating Officer,
whereby it has been held that the FBO/Supplier/Manufacturer have violated Sections 23(1), 26(1)
and 26(2)(ii) read with Section 3(1)(zf) of the FSS Act, 2006 and Regulation No. 2.2.1.3 and 2.2.2.10 of the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging & Labelling) Regulations, 2011, punishable u/s 52 of the FSS Act, 2006, therefore, the order of the Ld. Adjudicating Officer to this extent is upheld.
Section 52 of the FSS Act, 2006 reads as under:
"Penalty for misbranded food.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Packaging & Labelling) Regulations, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: (1) Any person who whether by himself or by any other person on his behalf manufactures for sale or stores or sells or distributes or imports any article of food for human consumption which is misbranded, shall be liable to a penalty which may extend to three lakh rupees.

(2) The Adjudicating Officer may issue a direction to the person found guilty of an offence under this section, for taking corrective action to rectify the mistake or such article of food shall be destroyed."
13.

The sample in the present case was taken in the year 2015 and the order was passed by the Ld.
Adjudicating Officer in February, 2019 and thereafter the appeal was filed before this Tribunal.
The supplier/manufacturer have already undergone the trauma of contesting the case for around five years.

In the facts and circumstances of the case and the submission of the Ld. Counsel for the appellants that the appellants have taken corrective action to rectify the mistake, I consider that a fine of Rs.1,00,000/ (Rupees One Lakh Only) upon M/s Tifosi Foods Pvt. Ltd. and fine of Rs.50,000/ (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) upon M/s Shellz Overseas Pvt. Ltd. shall meet the end of justice.
The manufacturer is also directed to take corrective action to rectify the mistake and shall also destroy the food article, if any, in the store.
The manufacturer shall also ensure that there is no such violation in future.
14. With the above observations, the present appeal is disposed of.

15. Record of the Ld. Adjudicating Officer along with copy of the judgment be sent and thereafter,
appeal file be consigned to Record Room.
